cover.verdict: Open, but not easy. Burgers are taken and legacy pizza is retreating. Chicken is the live window, and it narrows once KFC arrives, expected from 2027.

stats.label: restaurant prices above the EU average

market.headline: Rich, small and expensive, and it eats out less than you'd expect
market.intro: Norway has the spending power. What it lacks is eating-out frequency. The brands that win here sell value per visit and convenience, not the special occasion.

tiles.label: POPULATION
tiles.body: Measured at 1 July 2026, up from 5.59m at the end of 2024. Small by EU standards, so plan for a national footprint rather than a single city.

tiles.label: GDP PER HEAD
tiles.body: The 2024 figure. SSB puts it 63% above the EU average after adjusting for prices. Oil wealth inflates the total; mainland output grew 1.8% in 2025.

tiles.label: FOOD-SERVICE SPEND
tiles.body: Household spend on restaurants and accommodation in 2025, up 3.9% in volume. Food and drink serving alone accounted for NOK 104bn in 2023.

tiles.label: FRANCHISE COUNT
tiles.body: There is no public official count. The last government estimate, from 2011, was c. 300 systems and c. 25,000 franchisees. Virke sells a paid industry report.

tiles.label: CONSUMER SPENDING
tiles.body: Real household consumption growth in 2025. Confidence is still negative at −16.6 (Q3 2026), and restaurant and hotel prices are rising 6.0% a year, against 3.4% for everything.
tiles.src: NOU 2026:5 [S5] · Finans Norge [S6] · SSB CPI Sep 2026 [S11]

tiles.label: CURRENCY · NOK
tiles.body: €1 = NOK 10.49 and $1 = NOK 9.36 on 22 Oct 2026. Norges Bank raised the policy rate to 4.50% in September 2026 and says it may go higher.

market.eatsNote: Three facts that shape every unit P&L

eats.label: HOW OFTEN · RARELY
eats.body: eat out weekly, and around half do so less than once a month. The packed lunch (matpakke) still beats the lunch counter.

eats.label: AT WHAT PRICE · EXPENSIVELY
eats.body: Restaurant and hotel prices sat 40% above the EU average in 2024, and they are rising almost twice as fast as general inflation.
eats.src: Price level index, EU27 = 100. Eurostat prc_ppp_ind, 10 Jul 2025 [S10, S11]

eats.label: WHERE · IN OSLO
eats.body: spent per head eating out by Oslo residents, against about NOK 10,000 in the rest of the country. Oslo alone has 2,919 food-service outlets.
eats.src: NOK per head, approximate as published. Menon Economics for NHO Reiseliv, Jun 2025 [S12, S14]

market.sowhat: Margins are thin, at 2–3% EBIT across the sector in 2023–24, and visits are rationed. A concept that needs frequent, impulse visits to break even will struggle. One that earns a full basket per visit, or sits on a route people already travel, has room. [S12]

rising.headline: Burgers and chicken are growing. Legacy pizza is shrinking and coffee is flat.
rising.intro: A rise or fall call needs two independent signals. Where we found only one, the row is marked Thin. Unit counts come from brand locators (counted 23 Oct 2026) or the dated source shown.

rows.evidence: Fly Chicken grew from 11 to 19 sites. Apollo Group (KFC franchisee) agreed to buy it and convert most sites to KFC, with €20m over 5 years; the deal is subject to approvals. No other international chicken chain found.
McDonald's grew from 85 to 100 sites, with 7 more planned for 2026. Burger King went from 97 to "over 100".

Domino's fell from 47 to 43 sites and was loss-making in 2023 and 2024. Dolly Dimple's fell from 43 to 21 and is now out of Oslo. Against this, Peppes plans 50 new franchised sites and Pizzabakeren claims 200.
Jafs grew from 54 to "over 60"; Big Bite from 53 to "over 70". Current figures are brand claims, not counts.
Starbucks held at 22 sites. Espresso House revenue was flat at NOK 499–516m (2023–25). Waynes Coffee's Swedish parent went bankrupt in Jul 2026.
No trend data. Backstube lists 45 Norwegian units (undated). No international doughnut or dessert-parlour chain found.
Independents and micro-chains only (Oslo, Bergen). No international chain found.
Sabi Sushi grew from 9 to 42 sites and now reaches as far north as Tromsø. Subway appointed a new Nordic master franchisee in 2025, targeting 250 Nordic sites by 2032.
Grocery sales of meat alternatives peaked in 2021 and fell back to 2020 levels. No plant-based restaurant chain found.
McDonald's signed a roadside deal with the Esso network for 7 sites; its 100th site is on the E16. Commercial overnight stays hit a record 40.6m in 2025 (+5.2%).

chart.title: Change in unit count, selected chains
chart.note: Units added or lost over the window shown. Windows differ, so compare direction, not size.
chart.source: *Lower bound: brand says "over 100". Sources: brand locators counted 23 Oct 2026 (Sabi, Dolly Dimple's), brand releases, filings and press (S35–S52).

reading.title: Growth follows the national operator
paras: The growth is going to brands with a **national operator behind them**: McDonald's (14 franchisees), Burger King (King Food), and now KFC (Apollo Group).
Pizza is not dying. It is **consolidating** around the two domestic leaders, while weaker and international pizza brands lose ground.
Coffee is **full**. Starbucks has stood still, and convenience chains sell coffee at scale: Reitan runs 310 stores and Circle K 253. [S55]

white.headline: Four gaps worth a closer look, and one has a deadline
white.intro: A gap is a need with growing demand and no clear owner. The size of each one is our judgement of the prize for a new entrant: S, M or L.

gaps.title: The second chicken brand
gaps.gap: We found one sizeable chicken chain, and it is being turned into KFC. KFC takes the first rung; nobody holds the second.
gaps.evidence: Fly Chicken grew from 11 to 19 sites. The first KFC openings are expected in early 2027, per Fly Chicken's founder. No Popeyes, Wingstop or similar found. [S35, S36, S61]
gaps.suits: International chicken brands with multi-country franchise systems.
gaps.route: Master franchise with a Nordic multi-brand operator.

gaps.title: Roadside and forecourt QSR
gaps.gap: Long drives, record tourism, and fuel networks hunting for food partners.
gaps.evidence: McDonald's signed with Esso for 7 sites, and its 100th site is on the E16. Commercial overnight stays reached 40.6m in 2025, with foreign stays at 14%. [S37, S38, S57]
gaps.suits: Small-box and drive-thru formats with a fast, simple menu.
gaps.route: Area developer, or a partnership with a fuel or convenience operator.

gaps.title: Fast casual beyond Oslo
gaps.gap: Regional towns, where a branded unit can work on a small catchment.
gaps.evidence: Sabi Sushi grew from 9 to 42 sites, including Tromsø and Bodø. Pizzabakeren runs 200 sites on a catchment of 6,000–8,000 people. [S44, S51, S52]
gaps.suits: Compact, low-labour fast-casual concepts with a franchise-ready manual.

gaps.title: Bubble tea and treat drinks
gaps.gap: A trend category with independents but no branded chain.
gaps.evidence: Only independents and micro-chains found, and no international chain present. Demand data: Not found. [S56]
gaps.route: Master franchise, or direct franchise with one strong Oslo partner.

matrix.intro: Our assessment from the page 3 evidence. Position is judgement, not measurement.
matrix.note: Bakery and dessert are left off: too little data to place. Source: WRW Hospitality analysis of S35–S57.

position.quote: If I ran an international chicken brand right now, I'd be in a Norwegian master-franchise conversation this quarter.
paras: KFC's first conversions are expected in early 2027. Once it has scaled, the market will have a clear first rung and room for one challenger. The second brand in will hold that rung. The tenth will be fighting for space.
If I ran a pizza or coffee brand, I'd look elsewhere. Those categories are full, and the weaker chains are already losing sites.

regulation.headline: No franchise law, a firm wage floor, and a trade mark you must file separately
regulation.intro: Norway is easy to enter on paper and expensive to run in practice. Your contract does all the protecting, so write it well. Your labour model does most of the damage, so test it first.

rows.text: **None.** There is no franchise-specific law, mandatory disclosure or registration. General contract, marketing and competition law apply. We found no proposals for change in 2024–26.
File with Patentstyret: NOK 3,800 including one class, then NOK 1,000 per extra class. Allow about 3 weeks to 4 months. **An EU trade mark does not cover Norway.** The Madrid route is available.
Register with Mattilsynet before opening. Inspection "smiley" reports must be posted at the entrance.
Two municipal licences (serving and skjenkebevilling), with character checks, granted for up to 4 years. An annual fee is charged by volume; the Oslo minimum is NOK 6,600.
No state certification. Stunning before slaughter is mandatory, so non-stunned halal meat is imported under a 150-tonne yearly tariff quota.
VAT is 15% on takeaway food and 25% eaten in. Corporate tax is 22%. No withholding tax on royalties to an unrelated franchisor (15% applies only to related parties in low-tax countries).
An AS needs NOK 30,000 share capital. The general manager and half the board must live in the EEA (the UK is accepted).

tiles.label: TRADE MARK FILING
tiles.body: Patentstyret fee including one class. Your EU mark does not reach Norway.

tiles.label: VAT, TAKEAWAY VS EAT-IN
tiles.body: Set the channel mix early: it moves the price on every ticket.

tiles.label: WITHHOLDING ON ROYALTIES
tiles.body: For an unrelated franchisor. 15% applies only to related parties in low-tax countries.

wage.title: Model the unit at Norwegian wages before you model the royalty
wage.sub: What every NOK 100 of pay costs the employer
wage.method: 12% holiday pay (5-week agreement; 10.2% statutory), 2% minimum pension, and 14.1% employer NI (zone I) on pay, holiday pay and pension. Excludes the 16 days of employer-paid sick leave. [S28–S32]
wage.floorNote: Per hour, hospitality, over-20 entry rate, from 15 Jun 2025. The collective agreement rate is NOK 227.17 from 1 Jun 2026. [S33, S34]
wage.allInNote: **ESTIMATE** NOK 204.79 × 1.3 ≈ NOK 266 an hour, converted at £1 = NOK 12.52. [S7, S33]

regulation.advice: Confirm the position with a Norwegian adviser before signing.

route.headline: Pick the route that fits your size. Then price the risk.
route.intro: Each route trades control against capital and speed. The examples below show how brands have actually come into Norway.

routes.name: Master franchise
routes.seen: KFC via Apollo Group with MM Group (2026). Subway via Nordic Bites Group (2025). Starbucks via Dely. [S35, S48, S53]

routes.name: Area developer
routes.seen: Burger King under King Food, which took control of a large franchisee in 2025. [S38]

routes.name: Direct franchise
routes.seen: Domestic chains growing this way: Sabi Sushi, Pizzabakeren, Peppes. Hard to support from abroad. [S44, S45, S51]

routes.name: Company-owned launch
routes.seen: Max Burgers: 7 units in 2023, 8 in 2025. UK chain Leon left in 2021 after 2 sites. [S49, S50]

fits.label: EMERGING BRAND
fits.title: Master franchise
fits.body: Under c. 25 units and no overseas track record. A Norwegian multi-site operator brings the wage, licence and property know-how you can't buy remotely.

fits.label: MID-SIZE BRAND
fits.title: Area developer by region
fits.body: Proven in 2 countries. Split Oslo and the west coast and keep control of standards. The domestic leaders all scale through local owners.

fits.label: GLOBAL BRAND
fits.title: Nordic master partner
fits.body: Every recent international entry in our data runs through a regional multi-brand operator. Back a partner who can take Norway and its neighbours.

route.riskTitle: Price the risk before you price the franchise

risks.label: COSTS AND DEMAND
risks.body: Restaurant prices are up 6.0% a year and sector margins are 2–3%. Only 17% of operators call the market good (Oct 2026). Food-service bankruptcies were 87 in Q3 2026, down 9%.

risks.label: LABOUR
risks.body: A legal hospitality wage floor of NOK 204.79 an hour and about 30% on-costs. Model the unit at Norwegian wages before you model the royalty.

risks.label: SUPPLY CHAIN
risks.body: Norway is outside the EU customs union, and farm imports run on tariff quotas. Plan local meat and dairy; non-stunned halal is capped at 150 tonnes a year.

risks.label: SEASONALITY
risks.body: Summer and tourist routes peak hard: 40.6m commercial overnight stays in 2025, with foreign stays at 14%. Flex labour and site mix to match.

risks.label: REGULATORY
risks.body: With no franchise law, your contract carries all the protection. Alcohol licences are local and discretionary. Single-use plastics are banned, and packaging duties apply.

risks.label: CURRENCY AND RATES
risks.body: Royalties are earned in NOK. The policy rate is 4.50% and may rise, which squeezes franchisee borrowing for fit-outs.

days.headline: Ten moves, in order, before you sign anything
moves: **File your trade mark** with Patentstyret now. Your EU mark does not cover Norway.
**Search Patentstyret and Brønnøysund** for clashing names before you spend on a launch.
**Rebuild the unit P&L** at Norwegian wages, with about 30% on-costs.
**Set the takeaway and eat-in mix** early: 15% VAT vs 25%.
**Shortlist 3 to 5 Nordic multi-brand operators** as master or area partners.
**Prepare a full disclosure pack** anyway. No law requires one, but serious partners will expect it.
**Map local supply** for meat and dairy, including halal and import quotas.
**Choose your first cluster:** Oslo for spend, or one regional city for lower rents.
**Plan the licence path:** Mattilsynet registration, plus alcohol licences if needed.
**Agree how royalties are paid** and hedged in NOK.
